Trace:

```
[TRACE] store.ts addItem:enter item={id:'apple',price:2,quantity:1} items=[]
[TRACE] store.ts addItem:setItems newItems=[apple]
[TRACE] store.ts addItem:setTotal newTotal=2
[TRACE] CartView:render items=[apple] total=2

[TRACE] store.ts addItem:setItems newItems=[apple,banana]
```

evals.expected_output: The agent recognizes that the trace shows the SYMPTOM (total going NaN then 0) but does NOT show the CAUSE — i.e., why setTotal received NaN. The agent requests another round of [TRACE] logs to instrument the recalculateTotal function and the inputs flowing into it, instead of declaring a root cause like 'NaN coercion' or 'we need a NaN guard.' The agent stays in trace mode and does not propose a fix.
expectations: Identifies that the trace shows total transitioning from NaN to 0 (the symptom)
Recognizes that the trace does NOT show the cause of NaN — it shows setTotal receiving NaN but does not show what made the value NaN (the multiplication inputs, recalculateTotal internals, etc.)
Requests another round of [TRACE] logs at narrower scope — e.g. inside recalculateTotal, on the item.price/item.quantity values, or on what setTotal is being called with
Does NOT declare 'NaN coercion' or 'NaN guard' or similar surface-level pattern matching as the root cause based on this single round
